At least that's what I'm calling it.
So I'm back again with another issue - In essence, there is a ground layer of formulas that don't involve any updates. Then, a ground layer of action models which only contain such formulas. Then, the level above is formulas that only use those action models, etc etc.

However, through the restrictions on mutual blocks, it doesn't seem possible to reduce/increase the depth of the type. What follows are a MWE's of a few attempts to work within this. The fourth attempt (I believe) should work. However, it relies on an axiom, rather than built-in containment as part of the types. If there are better methods that don't just sidestep the issue, that would definitely be more interesting/preferred, so I wanted to ask other's opinions.

Edit: I should note that the precondition of states in an action model can contain updates from any action model lower in the heirarchy, not just directly underneath it. In that sense, the fourth is the only truly valid attempt, but I assume the concept is understandable.
If there was a way to have the axiom in Attempt 4 as a hypothesis within the ActionModel, that would work, but I can't define the function over which the axiom exists until I'm outiside of the block defining Form.

-- Attempt 1, Edge case for 0th depth
-- Closest to what I want conceptually, but furthest from working
mutual
inductive Form₁ (A : Type) (0 : Nat)
  | bot

inductive Form₁ (A : Type) (depth : Nat)
  | bot
  | update  (AM : ActionModel₁ A depth)
            (ϕ : Form₁ A depth)

structure ActionModel₁ (A : Type) (depth : Nat) where
  states : Type
  nzd : depth > 0
  pre : (s : states) → Form₁ A (depth - 1)
end

-- Attempt 2, undefined AM type to keep out of mutual
inductive Form₂ (A : Type) (d : Nat) (AM : Nat → Type)
  | bot
  | update (AMα : AM d) (ϕ : Form₂ A d AM)

structure ActionModel₂ (A : Type) (d : Nat) where
  states : Type
  nzd : d > 0
  pre : (s : states) → Form₂ A (d - 1) (ActionModel₂ A)

-- Attempt 3, counter within Form that keeps track of depth
mutual
inductive Form₃ (A : Type) (d : Nat) : Nat → Type
  | bot : Form₃ A d d
  | update (AMα : ActionModel₃ A d) (ϕ : Form₃ A d d) : Form₃ A d (d + 1)

structure ActionModel₃ (A : Type) (d : Nat) where
  states : Type
  pre : (s : states) → Form₃ A d d
end

-- 'Successful' Attempt 4
mutual
inductive Form₄ (A : Type) where
  | bot
  | update  (BMβ : ActionModel₄ A)
            (ϕ : Form₄ A)

structure ActionModel₄ (A : Type) where
  states : Type
  point : states
  pre : (s : states) → Form₄ A
end

def ActionModel₄.contains {A : Type} :
  (ActionModel₄ A) → (ActionModel₄ A) → Prop :=
  let rec loop : (Form₄ A) → (ActionModel₄ A) → Prop
    | Form₄.bot, _       => False
    | Form₄.update AMα ϕ, BMβ => AMα = BMβ ∨ loop ϕ BMβ
  fun (AMα BMβ) => ∃ (α : AMα.states) (β : BMβ.states),
                      (loop (AMα.pre α) {BMβ with point := β})

axiom AM_wf {A : Type} :
  IsWellFounded (ActionModel₄ A) (ActionModel₄.contains)

You probably meant it the other way, IsWellFounded (ActionModel A) (flip ActionModel.contains) is a theorem:

mutual
inductive Form (A : Type) where
  | bot
  | update (BMβ : ActionModel A) (ϕ : Form A)

structure ActionModel (A : Type) where
  states : Type
  point : states
  pre : (s : states) → Form A
end

def ActionModel.contains {A : Type} :
  (ActionModel A) → (ActionModel A) → Prop :=
  let rec loop : (Form A) → (ActionModel A) → Prop
    | Form.bot, _       => False
    | Form.update AMα ϕ, BMβ => AMα = BMβ ∨ loop ϕ BMβ
  fun (AMα BMβ) => ∃ (α : AMα.states) (β : BMβ.states),
                      (loop (AMα.pre α) {BMβ with point := β})

instance AM_wf {A : Type} :
    IsWellFounded (ActionModel A) (flip ActionModel.contains) where
  wf := by
    constructor
    intro a
    suffices ∀ pt, Acc (flip ActionModel.contains) { a with point := pt } by
      specialize this a.point
      cases a; assumption
    intro pt
    induction a using ActionModel.rec (A := A) (motive_1 := fun f => ∀ a pt,
        ActionModel.contains.loop f { a with point := pt } →
        Acc (flip ActionModel.contains) a) with
    | bot m pt hm => cases hm
    | update BMβ ϕ ih₁ ih₂ m pt hm =>
      rcases hm with rfl | hm
      · cases m with | mk _ pt'
        exact ih₁ pt'
      · exact ih₂ m pt hm
    | mk states point pre ih =>
      constructor
      intro y ⟨α, β, hr⟩
      dsimp at hr α
      exact ih α y β hr

Also, "nested mutual inductive type" already has a different meaning, specifically inductives like this:

mutual

inductive Thing where
  | foo (a : List OtherThing)

inductive OtherThing where
  | bar (a : Thing) (x : Nat)

end

where OtherThing is nested inside of List.

Isn't the flipped function saying "There exists an action model which contains this action model within one of it's states' precondition"?
My bad about the terminology, I wasn't sure what to call this - Inductive induction?

It doesn't seem possible to prove that "The precondition of all action models terminate" unless Lean fundamentally wouldn't allow the precondition of an action to contain another action within the same action model, or to loop at some point within heirarchy of action models.

If you really meant the other one, that's easy to disprove:

def seq (n : ℕ) : ActionModel A :=
  match n with
  | 0 => { states := Unit, point := (), pre := fun _ => .bot }
  | k + 1 =>
    { states := Unit, point := (), pre := fun _ => .update (seq k) .bot }

theorem not_AM_wf : ¬ IsWellFounded (ActionModel A) ActionModel.contains := by
  intro hwf
  have := hwf.apply _ (seq 0)
  generalize 0 = i at this
  generalize hx : seq i = x at this
  induction this generalizing i with | intro a h ih
  cases hx
  exact ih (seq (i + 1)) ⟨(), (seq i).point, .inl (by cases seq i; rfl)⟩ (i + 1) rfl

IsWellFounded (ActionModel A) ActionModel.contains means that there is no chain
"... contains a3 contains a2 contains a1 contains a0"
and you can easily provide an action model that contains a given action model.

I'm aware it's not true by construction, which is why I'm trying to restrict it through the axiom. I would prefer having a method through the structures, but I can't do it through this method since I can't reduce through Form to check it.

Actually, I may not even need to put it in the ActionModel:

structure WFActionModel (A : Type) where
  AMα : (ActionModel₄ A)
  AM_acc : Acc ActionModel₄.contains AMα

Should work?
The axiom would be inconsistent, that is, you could use it to prove 1 = 0; and WFActionModel is an empty type.
I don't really understand what you're trying to do with this axiom
You're sure that you didn't mean IsWellFounded (ActionModel A) (flip ActionModel.contains)?
I'm trying to say that "From now on, we assume this to be true" - Being that the only action models we are interested in are the ones that terminate in what action models they depend on
I think you've got it backwards. Acc ActionModel₄.contains AMα is always false.
Isn't ActionModel₄.contains AMα only true for an action model contained within the precondition of a state within AMα? (loop has its variables poorly named, AMα should be CM\gamma or something)

ActionModel₄.contains AMα BMβ means some { BMβ with point := b } is "inside" some AMα.pre s, so Acc ActionModel₄.contains AMα means if you start at AMα and at each step you ascend to a bigger ActionModel₄ (one that contains your current one) then you must eventually terminate. It is always false because of course there's nothing stopping you from going to bigger and bigger ActionModel₄s.

Oh sorry you're correct, Acc works backwards from how I thought - Conceptually the idea should be fine though, correct? As long as I call the function backwards?
Wait does that mean flipping the function is correct? But IsWellFounded shouldn't be provable for all ActionModels as a theorem.

I'm not sure why this is being so hard for me to visualise even when looking at the definition for Acc and WellFounded.

That's why I assumed the function was the other way around, proving that 'There is an action model which contains this one as the precondition of an one of its actions'

it's the same reason I can't define a natural number

def infty : Nat := Nat.succ infty
If you wanted to allow cyclic dependencies, you can't do it with inductives, you would need coinductives... which we don't directly support in Lean
Coinductives are essentially like inductives except they allow for elements that are infinitely deep
but inductives cannot be infinitely deep
